summary: [review:correctness] pendingClose treats a held-back close as spent only while closed.json exists, so deleting closed.json to reopen a feature brings the old held-back close back and a later satisfied /verify-build closes on an audit that never saw the new code
evidence: code-review finding 2: readRounds returns all rounds once closed.json is gone; last is still closeDeferred

summary: [review:correctness] a --resume run may close with --verified, setting audit.anchorCommit to HEAD although the resumed evidence may predate commits made since the interruption, so /ship-build custody skips re-proving them
[review:cost] a plain --resume re-runs Step 7.3s audit even when a held-back close from this run is still pending, spending one of the three audits
[review:consistency] the report Next line says the command that ran the check closes the feature, but /verify-build --no-fix, --criteria or --chained never close; readout and report then disagree
[review:correctness] the new same-session lock rule lets a --chained run leave implement.lock for its caller, but /verify-build and standalone /audit-build never release it
[review:altitude] the re-audit cap of 3 calls is copied into prose because MAX_REAUDITS is not exported; prompt and library can drift
[review:cleanup] the pending-close CLI repeats the run-id comparison pendingClose already does
